ingest.note: Analyzes 16kHz PCM frames in-process to detect speech segments.

egress.note: Passes PCM through unchanged. Emits speech detection events alongside.

latency_evidence.methodology: Callsmith architecture-budget placeholder; benchmark in the deployment region before setting an SLO.

interruption.description: Silero VAD detects user speech during agent output. When speech is detected and the agent is speaking, an interruption is triggered.
interruption.code_hint: Pipecat: SileroVADAnalyzer in LLMUserAggregatorParams. LiveKit: silero.VAD.load() in AgentSession vad= parameter.

potholes.note: Default min speech duration may cause false triggers from background noise. Tune confidence threshold (default 0.7) and min speech frames for your environment.
Silero model (~2MB) is downloaded on first use. In production, pre-warm it at startup to avoid cold-start delay on the first call.

Load one ONNX InferenceSession per worker process and reuse it forever. Re-initializing the model per call — or worse, per frame — stalls the audio hot path (tens to hundreds of ms) and surfaces as unexplained endpointing delay.

Silero consumes fixed windows (512 samples = 32 ms at 16 kHz). Buffer inbound frames and run inference once per window; running it per WebSocket message (arbitrary chunking) wastes CPU and corrupts speech-probability context.

Default ONNX Runtime threading on a multi-call worker causes CPU contention that appears as endpointing jitter at high concurrency. Set intra-op threads deliberately and cap concurrent calls per worker.
Reset VAD internal state on call end and after barge-in. Stale recurrent state causes phantom end-of-speech on the next utterance or the next call sharing the worker.

Run VAD exactly once. A framework turn detector (LiveKit silero.VAD.load(), Pipecat SileroVADAnalyzer) plus a second custom Silero instance doubles CPU and produces disagreeing endpoints. Pick one owner.

deployment.self_host_notes: Runs in-process inside the agent worker. Warm pool: pre-load one shared ONNX session per worker at startup and size concurrent calls per worker so VAD CPU never starves endpointing; see onnx_session_reuse and onnx_thread_contention potholes.
